description: Pack MULTIPLE small matrices per CTA at n=176/352 to fill the idle GPU. These shapes are latency-bound at very low occupancy (n=176 0.27 waves/SM, n=352 0.07, GPU 73-95% idle) because one CTA factors one matrix and there are only 40 matrices. Instead assign K matrices (e.g. 2-4) to each CTA — each warp-group factors a different matrix's panel concurrently within the same CTA, so a CTA's barrier-stall on matrix A overlaps with progress on matrix B, and the 40-matrix batch maps to 40/K CTAs but each does K-way independent work raising per-SM utilization. This is the small-matrix batched-factorization shape (one CTA, multiple matrices, warp-per-matrix or warpgroup-per-matrix) that MAGMA uses for tiny batched QR. Targets n=176 (~557us) and n=352 (~1424us); keep n>=512 as parent (6d356551). FP32. Validate the per-matrix correctness carefully (each matrix independent). No 'stream' substring; stock libs load_inline sm_100a.

TRIAL 1: pack KP matrices/CTA in the n=352 panel (panel_factor_packed_kernel<WGT,KP>, one warp-group of WGT threads per matrix, named bar.sync barid=wg+1 -- barid 0 is reserved for whole-CTA __syncthreads, using it with a partial count was an Illegal-instruction fault). Byte-identical (H,tau,V,T) per matrix vs single-CTA (maxdiff ~1e-5 vs torch.geqrf for KP=1..4, B=8/40). All 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. SAME-RUN A/B (contention identical, n=352 B=40): kp1(parent single-CTA)=5970us, kp2=6199us(0.963x), kp3=6443us(0.927x), kp4=11309us(0.528x); wgt128 variants similar. PACKING n=352 REGRESSES MONOTONICALLY with K. ROOT CAUSE (profile-confirmed): the single-CTA n=352 panel uses only ~51KB SMEM/CTA so ~4 CTAs co-reside per SM already (40 matrices=40 CTAs well-spread); packing RAISES per-CTA SMEM (KP=4 ~204KB) and LOWERS co-resident CTA count to 1/SM, so KP=4 is catastrophic. The brief's '0.07 waves/SM, 73-95% idle' premise does not hold for the n=352 BLOCKED-panel path (it holds for the n=176 full-matrix MEGAkernel at 124KB/1-CTA-SM). nsys: packed kp2 panel=34.5ms vs single-CTA 29.0ms. Benchmark geomean 11966us is under ~1.5x heavier contention than parent's 8190 (n512 sentinel 26611 vs 17674) so compare via the SAME-RUN A/B above, not raw geomean. OPEN: n=176 (still on the megakernel, untouched here) is the genuinely SMEM-starved 1-CTA/SM shape -- but 2 full 176x176 matrices=248KB>228KB cap, so packing there needs a panel-windowed (not full-matrix-resident) megakernel; OR pack the smaller-SMEM (34KB/matrix) n=176 BLOCKED panel. Next trials explore n=176 packing.

TRIAL 2 (comment-only; kernel byte-identical to trial 1, KP=2 n=352 packed): MATCHED-CONTENTION confirmation of the packing negative. This benchmark ran in the LIGHT-contention regime (n512 sentinel 17680 == parent baseline 17674), so the geomean IS comparable to parent's 8190: committed geomean 8325.9 (parent 1.017x faster). Contention-invariant ratios at matched contention: n352/n512 = 3487/17680 = 0.19724 vs parent 2888/17674 = 0.16338 (+20.7% REGRESSION); n176/n512 = 1176/17680 = 0.06654 vs parent 0.06655 (UNCHANGED, n=176 left on the megakernel). This exactly matches the same-run A/B (kp2=0.963x on n=352). TRIPLE-CONFIRMED packing negative: (1) same-run A/B n=352 kp1=5970/kp2=6199/kp3=6443/kp4=11309us and n=176 mega=2875/blkpack-kp2=2998/kp3=3074/kp4=3157us, both monotonic regressions; (2) nsys total-GPU-time kp2 panel=34.5ms vs single-CTA 29.0ms; (3) matched-contention benchmark ratio above. ROOT CAUSE: the brief's premise (0.07-0.27 waves/SM, GPU 73-95% idle) is FALSE for the BLOCKED-panel paths these shapes actually use -- the single-CTA n=352 panel is only ~51KB SMEM/CTA so ~4 CTAs co-reside per SM (40 matrices=40 CTAs well-spread); packing K matrices/CTA RAISES per-CTA SMEM (KP=4~204KB) and LOWERS co-resident CTA count to ~1/SM. The idle-GPU premise holds ONLY for the n=176 full-matrix MEGAkernel (124KB/CTA, 1 CTA/SM) -- but 2 full 176x176 FP32 matrices = 248KB > 228KB cap, so full-residency packing is structurally IMPOSSIBLE there, and the blocked-panel packing that DOES fit is itself slower than the megakernel (0.959x). Warp-group barrier overlap did NOT materialize as a win in any measured config.

Explored 'pack K matrices/CTA at n=176/352' over 2 committed trials + extensive same-run A/B sweeps. BUILT a packed panel kernel panel_factor_packed_kernel<WGT,KP> (KP matrices/CTA, one warp-group of WGT threads/matrix, per-warp-group named bar.sync barid=wg+1 + a warp-group-local block reduce; byte-identical (H,tau,V,T) per matrix vs the single-CTA panel, verified maxdiff ~1e-5 vs torch.geqrf for KP=1..4). All 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; no 'stream'; sm_100a; FP32.

RESULT = TRIPLE-CONFIRMED MEASURED NEGATIVE: packing REGRESSES both target shapes monotonically with K. (1) SAME-RUN A/B (contention identical): n=352 B=40 kp1(parent)=5970us, kp2=6199us(0.963x), kp3=6443us(0.927x), kp4=11309us(0.528x); n=176 B=40 mega(parent)=2875us, blkpack-kp2=2998us(0.959x), kp3=3074, kp4=3157us; cb=16 narrow-panel packing also regresses (n352 kp2 0.943x). (2) MATCHED-CONTENTION benchmark (n512 sentinel 17680 == parent 17674): ratio n352/n512 = 0.19724 vs parent 0.16338 (+20.7%); n176/n512 0.06654 unchanged (left on megakernel); geomean 8326 vs parent 8190. (3) nsys: packed kp2 panel 34.5ms vs single-CTA 29.0ms.

ROOT CAUSE (the brief's premise is FALSE for the path these shapes use): the brief's '0.07-0.27 waves/SM, GPU 73-95% idle' applies to the n=176 full-matrix MEGAkernel (124KB SMEM/CTA -> 1 CTA/SM). But (a) n=352 runs the BLOCKED panel at only ~51KB SMEM/CTA, so ~4 CTAs already co-reside per SM (40 matrices = 40 CTAs, well-spread) -- packing K/CTA RAISES per-CTA SMEM (KP=4 ~204KB) and LOWERS co-resident CTA count to ~1/SM, the opposite of the intent; (b) at n=176 the megakernel IS the SMEM-starved 1-CTA/SM case, but 2 full 176x176 FP32 matrices = 248KB > the 228KB cap, so full-residency packing is structurally impossible, and the blocked-panel packing that DOES fit is itself slower than the megakernel. Warp-group barrier-stall overlap did not materialize as a net win in ANY measured config (named-barrier warp-groups still contend for the SM's schedulers/SMEM).

COMMITTED HEAD c0451f1c routes n=352 through KP=2 (the least-bad packing, 0.963x) as the faithful measured result of the brief; n=176 unchanged (megakernel). The manager should NOT pick this as a parent for speed -- it is a characterized regression -- but the packed kernel + the occupancy law it establishes are reusable.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (surfaced, not pursued -- all OUTSIDE this brief's 'pack-K-per-CTA' objective): (1) The ONLY profile-identified lever at n=176 is LIFTING the megakernel's 1-CTA/SM occupancy (123.9KB > 114KB=228/2 blocks the 2nd CTA). A megakernel that does NOT keep the full matrix resident -- evict finalized columns [0,j) to global as R+v, hold only the active [j,n) window, dropping peak SMEM <114KB so 2 CTAs/SM fit -- is the untried structural variant (this is occupancy via windowing, brief 35's territory at n=1024, not packing). (2) A packed FUSED megakernel storing each matrix's working panel in BF16 SMEM (62KB -> 2 full matrices = 124KB fit) with FP32 math -- the only way to pack 2 FULL matrices at n=176 -- but the n=176 factor gate is tight (20*176*eps32 = 4.2e-4) and the brief constrained FP32, so this risks the gate (likely invalid; needs a measurement). (3) Raise MAXCB > 32 so the blocked path uses cb=44 (4 panels vs 6 at n=176/352), cutting launch count -- touches the shared C++ panel scratch buffers (red[MAXCB*16], wsh[MAXCB]) and ALL blocked-path n, so it is a cross-shape change. (4) CEILING REMINDER: n=176 and n=352 are each only ~3-4% of the 12-shape geomean and the parent is at/near each shape's per-shape optimum, so the headroom here is small; the big movers remain the n=512 B=640 (5 shapes) and n=1024 B=60 (4 shapes) groups.
